now.item: Walking skeleton. One out of hours request travels from a structured web form into the reservation office queue with a server written arrival time attached, end to end, English strings only. No model anywhere in it.
now.metric: Share of requests submitted through the form that carry a server written arrival timestamp, baseline zero because no published path records one today (c11), target 100 percent. Second reading, median time from arrival to a queue item an agent can act on, measured by the system rather than reported by anyone.
now.why_first: Highest cost of delay over the smallest job in the whole set. The guest's money sits on a 24 hour clock with a $10.00 per person penalty and forfeiture of all rights inside it (c12), while the only published route to act runs Monday to Friday, 7:00 AM to 3:00 PM Alaska Time and requires a phone call (c10, c11). Every night and weekend left in this season is capture nobody gets back. It is also the thinnest end to end slice, a form, a clock and a queue, so the whole path is proven before anything is added to it. OUR WORK, 3 to 5 working days, 3 if the field list and the queue destination are signed off at kickoff, 5 if the field list changes after the first look. WAITING ON YOU, one working session with Allyson Nannini or her delegate to fix the field list and the queue destination, then one sign off. WATCH IT RUN, sized in the counters item below rather than guessed at here. WHAT YOU PROVIDE, the field list, the queue destination, one named approver. TOP RISK, sign off lands on a five ship day when the approver is on the platform loading trains (c20, c30), which is the same collision the build exists to fix. MITIGATION, 3 business days of named slack against approver availability and nothing else, with the session booked before the build starts. YOUR OFF RAMP, stop here and you keep a working intake form, the timestamp and the queue, deterministic and running without us, with no licence and no per message cost.

now.item: A single governed source of the policy text, so the cancellation page, the product pages and every acknowledgement say the same thing about the hours, the 24 hour clock and the $10.00 per person penalty.
now.metric: Number of published surfaces that disagree on the cancellation hours or the penalty, baseline at least one real gap today because the hours sit on the product pages while the cancellation page states none (c10, c11), target zero. Second reading, every guest facing sentence about policy is a verbatim span from the approved file, asserted by a string containment check in code rather than by anyone's judgment.
now.why_first: It is a prerequisite rather than a nice to have, and there is no model in it at all. In Moffatt v. Air Canada the tribunal held the airline liable for what the automation on its own website said and rejected the argument that it was a separate entity (c44), so one governed source of policy text is the direct answer to that exposure. Point any answering layer at the site as it stands and the answer to when can I call to cancel is not on the cancellation page. OUR WORK, 2 to 3 working days to extract, structure and wire the file to the pages and the acknowledgement templates. WAITING ON YOU, one management or legal read of the extracted text, because we are republishing your policy and not writing one. WHAT YOU PROVIDE, the named owner of policy wording, plus any rule you apply in practice that the site does not carry. TOP RISK, the extract surfaces a rule that is applied and published nowhere, which turns a two day job into a policy decision that is yours and not ours. MITIGATION, we flag it in writing the day we find it and the build proceeds on the published text meanwhile. YOUR OFF RAMP, stop here and you keep the governed policy file and the corrected pages, which is worth having on its own even if nothing else is ever built.

now.item: An out of hours greeting on 1-800-343-7373 that states the published window and takes a callback request, producing the same timestamped record on the channel your guests' habit already lives on (c11). Telephony configuration, no model on the line.
now.metric: Out of hours calls that leave a timestamped callback record, baseline zero, target every call that reaches the greeting. Reported weekly beside the web and email counts, which makes the out of hours channel mix visible for the first time.
now.why_first: The phone is the published route for the highest stakes contact you have, so the cheapest real win on that channel is a greeting and a record rather than anything that talks back. A voice agent is refused outright and the refusal is written into the study rather than left implied. This item is small, independent and carries a third of the capture, so it ships in parallel with the form. OUR WORK, 1 to 2 working days of configuration. WAITING ON YOU, admin access to the phone system, or one call with whoever holds the carrier account. WHAT YOU PROVIDE, that access, and approval of the exact greeting wording, which we draft. TOP RISK, carrier side changes take as long as the carrier takes, and your phone provider is not something anyone outside the company can see, so we are estimating blind on that one edge. MITIGATION, 3 business days of named slack against carrier turnaround, and the web and email paths ship independently so this never blocks them. YOUR OFF RAMP, stop here and you keep the greeting and the callback log inside your own phone system.

now.item: A timestamped ingest on info@wpyr.com that queues the raw message unchanged, so an email arriving at 9pm on a Saturday carries a server written arrival time against the 24 hour cutoff.
now.metric: Share of inbound messages to that inbox that reach the queue with a server written timestamp and the original text preserved, baseline zero, target 100 percent. This counter doubles as the first measure of out of hours email volume that anyone has.
now.why_first: That inbox is where the unstructured survivor lives, and access to it is the longest pole in the whole phase, which is why the ask goes out on day one rather than when the build is ready for it. On the day we looked the ticketing system itself pointed customers at that inbox (c19), which is a point in time observation by three same day observers, could be transient, and is never presented as a standing condition. OUR WORK, 2 to 3 working days. WAITING ON YOU, a mail forwarding rule on info@wpyr.com set by whoever administers your mail. That is a small change on your side and the single item most likely to move the finish date. WHAT YOU PROVIDE, that rule, and a decision that raw guest messages may be stored unchanged. TOP RISK, mailbox access stalls and the remaining season runs out behind it. MITIGATION, we ask for a forwarding rule rather than credentials, we ask at kickoff, and the form and the greeting both capture without it. YOUR OFF RAMP, stop here and you keep the ingest and its log, and your inbox is untouched, because forwarding adds a copy rather than moving your mail.

now.item: Spanish and Japanese served as human translated fixed strings across the form, the greeting text and the acknowledgements, version controlled and re reviewed only when the policy changes.
now.metric: Language mix of inbound out of hours requests, a counter that does not exist today, plus a hard zero on machine translated money strings. Target, every policy sentence in all three languages traces to a named human translation of an approved span.
now.why_first: You state that you are actively seeking candidates fluent in Spanish and Japanese (c31), which is evidence the capability is wanted rather than evidence it is present, so there is no verified reader on your published directory to check an outbound machine translation. Runtime machine translation of any policy, price or refund text is therefore refused. c12 carries two clauses that are opposites separated by a preposition, a refund up to 24 hours prior minus the penalty and forfeiture within 24 hours, and a translation that swaps up to for within is a money misstatement on your own site in a language nobody on the published staff list is confirmed to read back. Inbound translation for agent comprehension stays allowed, with the original text always kept beside it, because the direction is what makes it safe. OUR WORK, 1 working day to wire the strings once they land. WAITING ON YOU, approval of the frozen string list, and a translator you trust or ours. WHAT YOU PROVIDE, that approval. TOP RISK, translator turnaround, 3 to 5 business days for a bounded string set and longer if the string list keeps growing. MITIGATION, the list is frozen before it goes out and English ships first, so capture starts without waiting on it. YOUR OFF RAMP, stop here and you keep the translated strings as files you own, usable anywhere on your site.

now.item: The four counters that do not exist today, produced as a by product of the agent doing the job they already do, at zero added workload, and labelled a shoulder season sample on the face of the readout.
now.metric: Four readings. Out of hours contact volume per week and the share closed without an agent touching them. Arrival time relative to the 24 hour cutoff, against a baseline of zero because there is no way to record one today. Language mix. Intent mix. Every one of these has a baseline of nothing published, so the phase one target is that they exist and are trustworthy, not that they hit a level.
now.why_first: The honest return of phase one is decision data first and cash second, and that ordering is the finding rather than a hedge. This is the item that makes the next spend computable instead of assumed. HOW THE WATCH IT RUN LANE IS SIZED, and this is the one place we can't hand you a number in advance. A pilot should be sized by real events rather than by round number weeks, and no contact volume is published anywhere for this company, no call count, no email count, no passenger count, no channel split, so anyone quoting you a pilot length in events today is inventing it. What we do instead. The first full week of live capture sets the run rate, we publish the event target the day that reading lands, and the first tuning pass is triggered by the earlier of the first 50 logged out of hours events or the second full week live. The window then closes on your own calendar, because the 2026 Summit season ends October 7, 2026 and there is not one more guest contact to observe after it until the next opening (c16). SHOULDER SEASON LABEL, and it rides with every number this phase produces. Bennett closes September 12, 2026 (c17), and the Summit season carries no service on May 2 to 4, on September 26 to 27, and on October 1 and 3 to 5 (c16), so a question mix measured this autumn describes a shoulder period and not a July peak. It may not be used to design 2027 without being re measured against the 2027 opening weeks, and that re measurement is written into the Next lane rather than left to good intentions. Note the eight weeks left to the close are calendar time, not observation time, because the build, the mailbox access and the phone configuration all come out of the same eight weeks. OUR WORK, 2 to 3 working days for the counters and the weekly readout. WAITING ON YOU, nothing beyond the agent resolving items the way they already do. WHAT YOU PROVIDE, that normal resolution, which is also the label, for free. TOP RISK, we read a shoulder season and someone treats it as the year. MITIGATION, the label is printed on the readout itself rather than in a footnote, and the 2027 re baseline is a gate condition.

now.item: Handoff and ownership. A runbook, the credentials, and a walkthrough with the reservation office, so the whole thing runs without us.
now.metric: The reservation office completes one change to the form fields and one change to a policy string unaided, watched and timed, before phase one is called done. Done is that demonstration, not a feeling.
now.why_first: Your published directory lists no technology lead, which is an absence rather than a fact about your capability, and its only legitimate use is to shape delivery toward managed, low maintenance builds rather than anything that assumes an in house engineer. So the phase ends with a system a non engineer can change. OUR WORK, 1 to 2 working days. WAITING ON YOU, one hour from the person who will own it. WHAT YOU PROVIDE, that person's name at kickoff rather than at the end. TOP RISK, the named owner is the same person the build exists to unload, and the walkthrough gets postponed into the season close. MITIGATION, the walkthrough is booked at kickoff onto one of your own published no service dates, September 26 or 27, or October 1, 3, 4 or 5 (c16), when no train is loading. YOUR OFF RAMP, there is nothing to stop after this one. You own everything built, with no licence, no model and no per message cost to keep it running.

next.item: Phase two, ONE model call on ONE node, classifying and extracting from the unstructured free text that arrives by email and in the form's free text box. Built in the off season, live before the 2027 opening. The arrival timestamp is written by the server before the model runs, so a total classifier failure degrades to today's behaviour plus a timestamp, a floor strictly above the status quo. No model ever states a refund outcome, prices anything or paraphrases the policy. The guest sees a verbatim span from the approved corpus or a human.
next.metric: Recall on the time sensitive money class, measured against the agent labels the 2026 capture produced for free, with an explicitly accepted false positive rate, because a false alarm costs an agent seconds while a missed Saturday night cancellation costs the guest the fare. The acceptance bar is written and agreed before the model is built, not after it is demonstrated. GATE, no labelled corpus large enough to hold out an evaluation set means no phase two. It waits for the 2027 season to produce one and nothing is billed for it meanwhile. Shipping a classifier in 2026 with no eval set would be a demo.

next.item: A written feasibility assessment of the third party ticketing vendor's API, run in the off season. A document, not a build. It is the thing that stands between you and a multi month commitment against an integration nobody has looked at.
next.metric: A yes or a no in writing, with the named auth method, the write scope, the rate limits and the vendor's stated support position. Delivered before the self service desk is scoped or priced, and the desk is neither until it comes back yes.

next.item: Re measure the four counters against the first weeks of the 2027 season before any 2026 reading is allowed to shape a 2027 design.
next.metric: The gap between the 2026 shoulder readings and the 2027 opening readings, published rather than quietly absorbed. If the gap is large, the 2026 numbers are retired as a design input and the readout says so in those words.

next.item: Buy the commodity answering layer if it fits you. An off the shelf tourism chat widget at published list pricing of $95 a month for 80 chats, $195 for 200 and $295 for 500, no fixed term contract, vendor configuration over one to four weeks (c48). We are not paid for this, it does not sit on our critical path, and you can start it whenever you like, including this season.
next.metric: A scripted probe set built from your own published pages, run before go live, asserting that every cancellation, refund and price question hands off to a human rather than answering it. Target, 100 percent handoff on those three classes. Two conditions ride with the recommendation and are not optional. One, it answers only published non money content. Two, under Moffatt the liability for what it says stays with you whoever built it (c44), and no vendor is going to open with that. Treat it as complementary rather than rival. It answers questions on the website, it does not create a timestamped work item against the 24 hour clock, and it does not touch info@wpyr.com, which is where the hard case lives. The named operator evidence is real and vendor published rather than independent, Black Cat Cruises reporting about 500 conversations a month, around 60 percent of questions answered and 10 hours a month saved (c47), where the 10 hours is the trustworthy figure, the modelled dollar number is never quotable as revenue, and Black Cat runs up to four daily departures against almost 2,000 train starts a season here (c7), so the direction transfers and the magnitude does not.

later.item: The deterministic self service change and cancellation desk. A guest opens a link, sees their departure, and changes or cancels it, with code applying your published rule exactly. No model is ever introduced onto this path, in any phase, for any reason, and that instruction attaches for the life of the build.
later.metric: Share of change and cancellation requests completed by the guest without an agent touching them, against a baseline of zero because there is no online path today (c11). Acceptance is exhaustive rather than statistical, every case either side of the 24 hour line, the $10.00 per person penalty arithmetic, the Alaska Time conversion and the forfeiture clause, all as unit tests, with any exception degrading to a timestamped work item in the same queue rather than to a wrong refund. GATE, the written vendor API assessment in the Next lane comes back yes first. TWO HONEST CAVEATS THAT STAY ATTACHED. There is a reach cap, guests who bought at a shore excursion desk sit in the cruise line's booking record and not in yours (c13). And the economics can cut against you in the short run, since a guest who can't reach anyone inside 24 hours forfeits the fare today (c12), so easier cancellation converts some forfeitures into refunds minus the penalty, and whether the resold seat covers that depends on your sell out rate by departure, which is not published (c14). You know that number and we do not.

later.item: Seasonal recruiting and onboarding across the three depots in two countries, carried here with its evidence asymmetry stated plainly rather than hidden. It has the best measured outside evidence in the entire study and the weakest local evidence.
later.metric: Time from application to a start date, which has no published baseline at this company, so the first work is measuring it rather than improving it. No time to hire, applicant volume, turnover figure or year round versus seasonal headcount split is published anywhere. The outside reading is Fortune reporting that Chipotle's time from application to first day dropped from 12 days to four after a conversational hiring assistant, with about 30 percent of scheduling work now happening after hours (c46), reported in Fortune's own voice rather than as an executive quote, and Chipotle is enormous so the direction transfers and the magnitude does not. HARD CONDITION, nothing here touches the terms, scheduling or monitoring of the roles inside the bargaining unit, because about 40 workers including tour guides, announcers and workers who greet visitors voted to join SMART-TD's local chapter on April 8 (c33), which is a negotiation before it is a deployment. Scope is confirmed against the unit in writing before any of it is designed.

later.item: First party post ride feedback capture, so what guests actually thought sits in your hands rather than on a platform you rent.
later.metric: First party verbatim comments captured per departure and the themes derived from them. Honest framing of the baseline, we hold zero verbatim customer reviews for you because every review platform returned HTTP 403 to every attempt, which is a limit on our study rather than a finding about you, so the baseline here is our blindness and not your silence. ONE HARD BOUNDARY, themes at the product and route level only, never individual staff performance, because the onboard roles are the ones inside the bargaining unit (c33).

later.item: Extend the governed policy file outward to the reseller and partner channels, so a season date or an exception date changes in one place and every desk shows it the same day.
later.metric: Number of partner or reseller surfaces showing a season or exception date that disagrees with the governed file, baseline unknown. CONDITION, the reseller evidence was not re verified this pass (c50), so this starts with a re check of those pages rather than with a build, and any specific price from them is re checked before it is used. The corroborated half is your own product appearing on a cruise line shore excursion page (c13). Unglamorous, real, and mostly a content governance job rather than an AI one, which is why it sits here and not higher.

later.item: An internal reply drafting aid for the reservation office, deferred rather than dropped. A human sends every word, so there is no guest facing exposure on it.
later.metric: Agent edit distance and time to send, both of which need a baseline that does not exist today, so phase one has to produce it first. TWO PERMANENT EXCLUSIONS. Outbound Spanish and Japanese generation stays off it, because a review path with no verified reviewer is an approval click rather than a review. Booking context assembly stays off it while the ticketing integration is unassessed. Worth naming the counter argument against this whole item, the biggest differentiator in the research is workflow redesign, which cuts against an assistant bolted beside an unchanged workflow.

later.item: Monitoring plus a deterministic fallback capture on the online buy door, so a guest who arrives at a closed door leaves a structured, priced, contactable intent instead of a bounce.
later.metric: Bounced checkout sessions converted into a captured intent. CONDITION AND MANDATORY CAVEAT, on 2026-08-09 the ticketing system returned an unavailable message pointing customers at the phone line and info@wpyr.com while the same page rendered an order processing thank you (c19). That is a point in time observation by three same day observers, it could be transient, and it is never presented as a standing condition. This is only worth building if your own uptime record says it is a pattern, and AI is close to the wrong answer for all of it, which is why it is not proposed as one.

later.item: Train scheduling against ship arrivals, parked on the map with its reason rather than pitched.
later.metric: None until a trains per day figure and a passenger count exist, and neither is published. Almost 2,000 train starts run through the summer season (c7) against five ships listed arriving in Skagway on one August Sunday (c20, a third party schedule aggregator at medium confidence), and this is a solver problem rather than an AI one. It stays here as a candidate for the day you can hand over that data.

later.item: Shore excursion settlement and reconciliation, a buy evaluation and not an Alaska AI build.
later.metric: None from us, and that is the finding. Shoretime is built specifically to run cruise shore excursion operations end to end, partnered with Norwegian Cruise Line Holdings since February 20, 2024, and it makes no artificial intelligence claim anywhere on its site (c41). The people closest to this exact workflow, with every commercial incentive to say AI, are not saying it, so the measure is whether a purpose built platform beats anything we would write, and we think it does.

later.item: REFUSED, a voice agent on the 1-800 line. It is not in any lane of this roadmap, and it is not a later phase either.
later.metric: No metric, because none can honestly be stated. No call volume is published to size or evaluate against, no recordings, transcripts or intent taxonomy exist, per turn compounding and latency both stack against it, and Moffatt exposure lands hardest on the highest stakes contact you publish (c44, c11). The narrow real win on that channel is the out of hours greeting in the Now lane, which is a phone system configuration and carries no model at all.

later.item: REFUSED for now, revenue management or dynamic pricing, with the condition that would ever change it written down.
later.metric: No passenger count, no load factors, no trains per day and no channel split are published, so there is no demand signal to model, which makes this the largest theoretical upside in the map and the least buildable thing in it. Amtrak's ARROW achieved an average additional revenue of 3 to 5 percent (c43), a real precedent and not a substitute for your own data. CONDITION, it would need your own demand history first, and a commercial conversation before an algorithmic one, because pricing is negotiated with cruise lines one of whose parent is a minority partner in the ownership group (c5).

later.item: REFUSED, predictive maintenance on the locomotive fleet. Proposing it would be inventing a need.
later.metric: None. Six 30 class engines currently in Skagway with the seventh and eighth due in 2026 (c36) is the entire evidence base, and no telemetry, no failure history and no cited maintenance pain appears anywhere in this study. Predictive maintenance is a genuine rail category, which is exactly why it is worth saying out loud that there is not one line of evidence here to build it on.

later.item: REFUSED, anything touching the terms, scheduling or monitoring of the represented workforce. This is a guardrail on the map rather than an opportunity on it.
later.metric: None, in any lane, at any phase. About 40 workers including tour guides, announcers and workers who greet visitors as they leave their cruise ships voted to join SMART-TD's local chapter on April 8 (c33). Reservation Agents are not among the roles that article names, which is why phase one appears clear of it, and absence from a list is not proof of non representation, so it is confirmed with you in writing at Gate 0 before anything ships.

gates: Four gates, each one framed as YOUR off ramp rather than ours. You can stop at every one of them and keep what has been built, because nothing in phase one carries a licence, a model, an inference bill or a per message cost. GATE 0, before we build anything, and it costs nothing. Three confirmations. One, in writing, that Reservation Agents sit outside the SMART-TD unit, since absence from the roles named in the April article is not proof of non representation (c33). Two, a named policy owner and a named approver who is not on the platform when we need them. Three, your decision on the honest complication, which is the thing a proposal showing only the upside would bury. Today a guest who can't reach anyone inside 24 hours forfeits all rights to a refund and you keep the fare (c12). A path that lets that same guest cancel at 9pm on a Saturday converts some of those forfeitures into refunds minus the $10.00 per person penalty. The offsetting gain is the resold seat on a ride that usually sells out in advance (c14), plus fewer disputes and less goodwill damage, and which effect is larger depends on your sell out rate by departure, which is published nowhere, so you know it and we do not. If that trade is not one you want, the roadmap stops at Gate 0 and it has cost you nothing. GATE 1, the skeleton is live. The bar is three demonstrations, not an opinion. One real out of hours request travels from the form to the queue with a server written arrival time, one from the phone greeting, and one from the inbox. Your off ramp, stop here and you keep the form, the timestamp, the queue, the greeting, the ingest and the governed policy file, all deterministic, all yours, all running without us. GATE 2, the season close, and this is the funding gate for phase two with its bar stated in advance rather than negotiated afterwards. Three conditions, all measured. One, at least one full week of clean capture across all three intake points with no missing timestamps. Two, an agent resolution recorded on every captured item, which is the label, and it costs nothing extra because it is the work they already do. Three, a labelled corpus large enough to hold out an evaluation set, where the size that means is computed from the observed run rate after the first week rather than asserted today, because no contact volume is published for this company and a number quoted now would be invented. If the season closes without that corpus, phase two does not start and is not billed, it waits for the 2027 season to produce one. There is a fourth condition and it cuts against us, so it stays in. If the counters show that out of hours arrivals are rare and your published window already covers nearly everything, the readout says exactly that, the roadmap stops, and you keep phase one and the numbers that ended it. That is the right way for us to lose this argument if we are wrong. GATE 3, the ticketing vendor. The self service change and cancellation desk is not scoped, priced or promised until the written API assessment comes back yes with a named auth method, a write scope and rate limits. No yes, no build, no spend. WHAT PHASE ONE COSTS IN OUR DAYS, 12 to 19 working days of engineering across the seven Now items, decomposed rather than aggregated so you can see where each day goes. The ranges close toward the low end when the field list, the mail forwarding rule and the phone access all land in the first week, and toward the high end when approvals fall on five ship days. The only slack in the plan is 3 business days against carrier turnaround and 3 business days against approver availability. Both are named, and there is no unnamed padding anywhere in this document.
high_integrity_dates: October 7, 2026, the published close of the 2026 Summit season (c16). This is your calendar rather than our promise, and it is the hardest constraint in the plan, because after it there is not one more guest contact to observe until the next opening. Our commitment staked against it, every capture surface is live before that date or the 2026 sample is zero, and the phase one measurement readout is in your hands within 5 working days of the close. The eight weeks between now and it are calendar time and not observation time, since the build, the mailbox access and the phone configuration all come out of the same eight weeks, and everything captured inside them is a shoulder season sample.

September 12, 2026, the published close of the Bennett Scenic Journey season (c17). Our commitment, every counter reading after that date is marked Summit only on the readout, so nobody later reads a Bennett number that could not have existed. The same treatment applies to your published no service dates, September 26 to 27 and October 1 and 3 to 5 (c16), which are excluded from any per day rate rather than silently averaged into one.

The 2027 opening date is deliberately NOT on this list, and the omission is the commitment. The 2026 Summit season opened April 30 (c16) and no 2027 opening date is published anywhere we could fetch, so a late April 2027 date from us would be an inference dressed up as a promise. What we stake instead, anything built for 2027 is in place and tested no later than 10 working days before your first published 2027 departure, and that clock starts the day you publish it.
